FRENCH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening.

2. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Thank you
   B. Good night only
   C. Excuse me
   D. Good morning / hello

3. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

4. When practising Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

5. When practising Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading.

6. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.

7. When practising Persuasive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive Speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive Speaking.

8. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.

9. When practising Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

10. When practising Reading for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for information.

11. When practising Informative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Informative Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Informative Speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Informative Speaking.

12. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. livre
   B. fenêtre
   C. chaise
   D. porte

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Critical Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Descriptive writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Expository writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Descriptive writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Process Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Expository Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Persuasive writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
